Day 2 Meteor Garden tour: Zhongshe flowers and the F4 campus

DateSun Apr 25EffortLong (12 hours, mostly sitting)

25Sun · Apr

Book on Klook: "Chiayi One-Day Tour: Iconic Meteor Garden Scenes (from Taipei)" (4.9★ from 862 reviews). It's one coach all day, so there are no changes and no buses to find. Times with ~ are my estimates; follow the times on your voucher.

  • Price: about ₱4,187 / NT$2,147 per person (seen Nov 22, 2026, during a 30%-off promo). Check before you go Entry to every stop is included; meals are not.
  • Runs: every day, with at least 6 people, so your 9 is enough.
  • It's a long ride: Chiayi is about 3 hours south. This is the same kind of distance as Sun Moon Lake, but on one bus instead of MRT, train and bus changes.

If the forecast 3 days before is very wet, ask Klook about moving to Tue Apr 27 and swap with Day 4.

Day 3 North Coast tour: Yehliu, Shifen, Jiufen

Pick a tour where Jiufen is the LAST stop, so you're there when the lanterns come on.

Why not a private van?

A 9-seater van legally carries only 8 passengers. Your 9 would need 2 cars or a bigger van, which usually costs more per person than the shared tour.

Doing it yourselves (skips Yehliu)

  1. Regular train (TRA) from Taipei Main to Ruifang, about 45–60 min.
  2. Pingxi Line day pass (₱156 / NT$80) to Shifen and back.
  3. 3 taxis from Ruifang to Jiufen.
  4. Bus 1062 back to Taipei (Zhongxiao Fuxing station).

It's doable but tiring with 9 people, which is why I'd pay for the tour.

Why this plan

That's 4 nights. Stay in one hotel in Ximending the whole time, so nobody has to repack.

What was wrong with your Day 2: Sun Moon Lake is about 3 hours each way (MRT, then the high-speed train, then a bus). In this plan the only long ride is the Day 2 Meteor Garden tour, and that's one coach from Taipei Main with no changes.

The five days at a glance
DayDateThemeEffort
1Sat Apr 24Arrive, Longshan Temple, nap, Dihua Street, river sunset, Ningxia night marketEasy
2Sun Apr 25Meteor Garden tour: Zhongshe flower farm and the F4 campus (National Chung Cheng University), one coach all dayLong (12 hours, mostly sitting)
3Mon Apr 26North Coast tour: Yehliu, Shifen sky lanterns, Jiufen at duskHardest (stairs)
4Tue Apr 27CKS Memorial Hall, Yongkang Street lunch, Taipei 101 / Elephant Mountain, Raohe night market, pasalubongMedium
5Wed Apr 28AirportEarly start

Why the days are in this order

  • Jiufen is on a weekday (Monday). Weekends there are the worst. Reviewers also say Monday crowds are "noticeably lighter".
  • The Meteor Garden tour is on Sunday. It runs every day, so it takes the weekend and leaves the two weekdays for Jiufen and the city.
  • The city day is on Tuesday. Din Tai Fung and Taipei 101 have shorter lines on a weekday, and the last evening stays light for pasalubong and packing.

Rain rule: if Sunday looks very wet, move the tour to Tuesday and do Day 4 on Sunday. The city day works fine in rain because the malls, 101 and Din Tai Fung are all indoors.

What I changed from your idea

  • Dropped Sun Moon Lake (the long travel day).
  • Fewer rides on Day 4: breakfast is at a Yonghe Soy Milk near the hotel instead of the Michelin-listed Fu Hang, which was out of the way and had a 30–60 min queue. The day now has 5 rides instead of 6.
  • Fixed the 12 noon check-in. Taipei hotels usually check in at 3 PM, so drop your bags at noon and nap at 3.
  • Replaced the Ximending "night market". Ximending is a shopping street. Instead you get two real night markets: Ningxia (mostly food) and Raohe (the best all-rounder). Ximending is still outside your hotel door every night.
  • Replaced Ichiran. It's a Japanese ramen chain. Have Taiwanese beef noodles instead.
  • Replaced Yangmingshan and Beitou (Day 2) with the Meteor Garden tour: the flower farm and the F4 campus you asked for, on one coach with no changes. That drops Qingtiangang, the calla lilies, Beitou's museum and hot springs, and Shilin night market.
  • Fit the ₱30k all-in budget (flights, hotel, pasalubong and everything else): a budget hotel at about ₱780 / NT$400 each a night, one eSIM per 3 people, lunch on Yongkang Street with Din Tai Fung optional, and food at about ₱1,268 / NT$650 a day. The Meteor Garden tour stays.
  • Kept the North Coast tour, Taipei 101, Carrefour and Yonghe soy milk.

  • The "Est. ₱ each" costs in the day schedules add up to about ₱16,670. The rest of the ₱17,880 covers drinks, snacks and extra taxis.

Before you fly

  1. Visa: Philippine passport holders can visit Taiwan visa-free for up to 14 days, and this has been extended to Jul 31, 2027, so your trip is covered. Each passport should be valid for 6+ months.
  2. Taiwan Arrival Card (TWAC): all 9 fill it in online at twac.immigration.gov.tw within 3 days before arrival (Apr 21–24). There are no paper cards anymore. It's free, so any site asking for money is a scam.
  3. Hotel: book now with free cancellation. Saturday nights in April fill up.
  4. Tours: the Meteor Garden tour for Sun Apr 25 (Klook; it needs at least 6 people, so your 9 is enough) and the North Coast tour for Mon Apr 26 (Klook, from Ximen). Book both 1–2 months ahead and check the cancellation terms. Many North Coast tours have free cancellation up to 24 hours before.
  5. EasyCard for each person (Klook airport pickup, or the 7-Eleven / Airport MRT counter at T1). Load ₱975 / NT$500 to start.
  6. eSIM (5-day unlimited) for at least 3 phones, one per group of 3 (see Group tips).
  7. Cebu Pacific baggage: check what 5J 313 includes. If you expect heavy pasalubong, add checked baggage online before the trip. It's usually cheaper than paying at the airport counter.
  8. Cash: night markets are cash only. Plan on about ₱1,170–1,365 / NT$600–700 per person per day. Bring USD or some TWD from Manila, and change a first batch at the bank counters in the T1 arrivals hall.
  9. Power: Taiwan runs on 110V. Phone and laptop chargers are fine. Philippine hair dryers and straighteners (220V) may not work, so check the label.
  10. "Lucky Land" ₱9,750 / NT$5,000 draw: the current round only covers travel up to Mar 31, 2027, and only for people who have visited Taiwan before. Check 5000.taiwan.net.tw in case it gets extended.

Where to stay

  • Area: Ximending, within a 5–7 minute walk of Ximen MRT. From there:
    • The airport train is 1 stop away (via Beimen).
    • Some North Coast tours leave from Ximending.
    • The 24-hour Carrefour is an 11-minute walk.
    • Food is everywhere.
  • Rooms: 2 quad rooms + 1 double, 3 triples, or a family room for 5 + a quad (no empty beds, so the cheapest per person).
  • Target: about ₱7,020 / NT$3,600 a night for all 9, which is ₱780 / NT$400 per person per night. That's budget-hotel level, and it's what fits the ₱30k all-in budget.
  • Check before you goPlaces with family or quad rooms in 2026 listings. Prices move, so check your dates. (US$ converted at NT$32.97, Wise, Nov 22, 2026.)
    • Ximen Holiday Fun Hotel: quad, about US$46 a night in an April 2026 listing. That's about ₱2,964 / NT$1,520, or ₱741 / NT$380 each when 4 share, so it fits the target.
    • Ximen Triple Tiger Hostel: standard triples and quads, plus family rooms for 5, 6 or 8 (no price in the listing I saw)
    • amba Taipei Ximending: family quad, about US$74 a night in a May 2026 listing. That's about ₱1,190 / NT$610 each when 4 share, so it's over the target.
    • Hotel Papa Whale: large family rooms, across from the main Ximending strip
    • Art'otel Ximending and Solaria Nishitetsu Ximen: family quads, more expensive
  • Search filters: elevator, rating 8.5+, free cancellation, room type "quadruple" or "family".
  • Avoid unlicensed Airbnb apartments. Short-term rentals without a licence are illegal in Taiwan and can get cancelled at the last minute.

Getting around

  • EasyCard: tap in and out on the MRT, buses and local trains, and pay at 7-Eleven. One card per person. The card costs ₱195 / NT$100.
  • Google Maps directions work well for Taipei's MRT and buses.

The MRT lines you'll use

  • Green: Ximen ↔ Beimen (connects to the airport train) ↔ Zhongshan ↔ Nanjing Sanmin ↔ Songshan (Raohe). Ximen ↔ CKS Memorial Hall is also 2 stops direct on green.
  • Blue: Ximen ↔ Taipei Main ↔ Shandao Temple; Ximen ↔ Longshan Temple.
  • Red: Taipei Main ↔ Jiantan (Shilin) ↔ Beitou → Xinbeitou; CKS Memorial Hall ↔ Dongmen ↔ Taipei 101 ↔ Xiangshan (Elephant Mountain).
  • Purple (Airport MRT): A1 Taipei Main ↔ T1. The Express train takes about 35 minutes and costs about ₱312 / NT$160. The Commuter train takes about 50 minutes.
  • Taxis: about ₱166 / NT$85 to start, then roughly ₱49 / NT$25 per km, plus ₱39 / NT$20 between 11 PM and 6 AM. The Uber app books these same taxis, max 4 people per car.
  • MRT rules: no eating, drinking or gum past the gates (fines can reach several thousand NT$). Stand on the right on escalators.

What reviewers agree on

  • Jiufen: go on a weekday. Tour buses arrive between 1 and 4 PM and the alleys turn into "a slow human conveyor belt". It's at its best after the lanterns come on around dusk. There are lots of stairs.
  • Night markets: Raohe is the usual first pick: compact, with the famous pepper buns. Ningxia is almost all food and less crushed than Shilin. Shilin is the biggest and most touristy, and gets hard to move through after 8 PM.
  • North Coast tour: the most-booked Klook version (Yehliu + Jiufen + Shifen + Golden Waterfall) is rated 4.9★ from over 48,000 reviews. Reviewers like that it fits three far-apart places into one day, which is hard to do yourselves. If people get tired, Shifen is the stop to cut first.
  • Meteor Garden tour: rated 4.9★ from 862 Klook reviews. Reviewers praise the guides for keeping the long day smooth and on time.
  • Uber in Taipei just books ordinary licensed taxis, which take at most 4 people. 9 people = 3 cars.

Tips for a group of 9

  • Split into 3 groups of 3, each led by one of the 20-somethings with mobile data and Google Maps. Each group = one taxi.
  • Restaurants: ask for 2 tables (4 + 5); you'll be seated much faster.
  • Night markets: each group buys 2 dishes and everyone shares, so you taste more for less.
  • Money: keep one cash pot for shared costs (taxis, lanterns) and track the rest in a shared expense app.
  • Hotel address: everyone keeps a screenshot of the hotel's address in Chinese for taxi drivers.
  • Stairs: comfortable shoes. The only real stair climbs are Jiufen and Elephant Mountain, and both are skippable.
  • Weather (El Niño year): NOAA expects a very strong El Niño this winter that is still going, but weakening, in April 2027. In Taiwan that usually means a wetter spring, though not every time. A normal April in Taipei is about 19–26°C, with rain on about 14 days of the month. Pack a folding umbrella, a light rain shell, quick-dry shoes with grip and spare socks, and check the CWA forecast 3 days before.
